title: Resilience Libraries: Polly and Hystrix
description: Learn to use popular resilience libraries Polly for .NET and Hystrix for Java.

data.text: Resilience libraries provide battle-tested implementations of resilience patterns. Netflix Hystrix pioneered resilience patterns for Java, while Polly is the de facto standard for .NET. Both libraries offer circuit breakers, retries, timeouts, and fallbacks.

Polly is a .NET resilience and transient-fault-handling library. It provides fluent APIs for circuit breakers, retries, timeouts, bulkheads, and fallbacks. Polly is widely used in .NET microservices and integrates seamlessly with HttpClient and ASP.NET Core.

Netflix Hystrix was one of the first resilience libraries, created to handle failures in Netflix's microservices. It provides circuit breakers, thread pool isolation, fallbacks, and a real-time dashboard for monitoring. Hystrix is now in maintenance mode; Netflix recommends resilience4j for new Java projects.

data.title: Polly vs Hystrix Comparison
items: Polly: .NET-native, fluent API, active development, supports async/await
Hystrix: Java-first, thread pool isolation, dashboard, now in maintenance mode
resilience4j: Modern Java alternative to Hystrix, functional style
Both implement the same core patterns: circuit breaker, retry, timeout, fallback

data.title: resilience4j
data.text: resilience4j is a modern Java resilience library that inspired Polly. It provides functional interfaces, annotation support, and integrates with Spring Boot and Micrometer for metrics.

items.question: Should I use a resilience library or implement patterns myself?
items.answer: Always use a library. Resilience patterns are subtle and error-prone. Polly, resilience4j, and Hystrix are battle-tested and handle edge cases you might miss.

items.question: Can I use multiple resilience libraries?
items.answer: Avoid mixing libraries. Choose one per project to keep complexity manageable. Polly and resilience4j cover most use cases.

items.question: How do I monitor resilience patterns?
items.answer: Use metrics libraries like Micrometer or App Metrics. Polly and resilience4j integrate with these to expose circuit breaker state, retry counts, and timeout metrics.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use resilience libraries instead of implementing patterns yourself
Polly is the standard for .NET; resilience4j for Java
Combine multiple patterns for comprehensive resilience
Monitor circuit breakers and retries with metrics
data.takeaway: Resilience libraries provide production-ready implementations; use them in all microservices.
